sentences.cn_text: 今年恰逢著名风景摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊拍摄的一系列黄石照片问世150周年。
sentences.en_text: This year marks the 150th anniversary of a series of Yellowstone photographs by the renowned landscape photographer William Henry Jackson.

sentences.cn_text: 他拍下了提顿山、老忠实泉和科罗拉多落基山脉等标志性景观的首批影像。
sentences.en_text: He captured the first-ever shots of iconic landmarks such as the Tetons, Old Faithful and the Colorado Rockies.

sentences.cn_text: 这些照片是杰克逊在19世纪晚期一次穿越黄石盆地的探险中拍摄的，该探险由美国领土地质与地理调查局局长费迪南德·V·海登率领。
sentences.en_text: Jackson snapped them on a late 19th-century expedition through the Yellowstone Basin that was conducted by the head of the U.S. Geological and Geographical Survey of the Territories, Ferdinand V. Hayden.

sentences.cn_text: 团队成员还包括一名气象学家、一名动物学家、一名矿物学家和一名农业统计学家。
sentences.en_text: The team included a meteorologist, a zoologist, a mineralogist, and an agricultural statistician.

sentences.cn_text: 两个世纪前，对许多美国定居者而言，「保护自然而非开发自然」的理念还是十分新颖的想法。
sentences.en_text: Two centuries ago, the idea of preserving nature, rather than exploiting it, was a novel one to many U.S. settlers.

sentences.cn_text: 而促使公众转而支持土地保护事业——尤其是认识到黄石地区之壮美——的转折点之一，正是这些生动的照片。
sentences.en_text: One of the turning points in public support for land conservation efforts — and recognizing the magnificence of the Yellowstone region in particular — came in the form of vivid photographs.

sentences.cn_text: 作为一名精于运作的华盛顿人士，海登意识到自己可以借助此次探险中令人震撼的视觉影像。
sentences.en_text: As an effective Washington operator, Hayden sensed that he could capitalize on the expedition’s stunning visuals.

sentences.cn_text: 他让杰克逊冲印出大幅照片，连同莫兰的画作复制品一并分发给每一位国会议员。
sentences.en_text: He asked Jackson to print out large copies and distributed them, along with reproductions of Moran’s paintings, to each member of Congress.

sentences.cn_text: “这些视觉影像，尤其是那些照片，真正让人切身感受到这是必须加以保护的地方，”墨菲说道。
sentences.en_text: “The visualization, particularly those photographs, really hit home that this is something that has to be protected,” says Murphy.

sentences.cn_text: 旅途中，杰克逊借助“湿版摄影法”同时操作多台相机及不同尺寸的底片，这种方法需要先在底片上涂覆化学药剂，再进行曝光，并在便携暗房中显影成像。
sentences.en_text: Throughout the trip, Jackson juggled multiple cameras and plate sizes using the “collodion process” that required him to coat the plates with a chemical mixture, then expose them and develop the resulting images with a portable darkroom.

sentences.cn_text: 这种原始的技术要求凭经验估算曝光时间，且所用设备笨重不便，须由数人合力搬运。
sentences.en_text: The crude technique required educated guesses on exposure times, and involved heavy, awkward equipment — several men had to assist in its transportation.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管困难重重，杰克逊仍拍下了数十张令人惊叹的照片，既有他那张如今已声名远扬的老忠实泉快照那样气势恢宏的画面，也有探险队员们在营地的随性肖像。
sentences.en_text: Despite these challenges, Jackson captured dozens of striking photos, ranging from majestic images like his now-famous snapshot of Old Faithful, to casual portraits of expedition members at the camp.

sentences.cn_text: 以往探险的老手们虽曾在文字中细述沿途壮丽景色，但这些生动的照片带来的却是截然不同的震撼。
sentences.en_text: While veterans of previous expeditions wrote at length about stunning trail sights, these vivid photographs were another thing entirely.

sentences.cn_text: 此次旅程于1871年6月8日在犹他州奥格登正式启程。
sentences.en_text: The journey officially began in Ogden, Utah on June 8, 1871.

sentences.cn_text: 在将近四个月的时间里，数十人骑马进入蒙大拿州，沿黄石河及黄石湖周边一路跋涉。
sentences.en_text: Over nearly four months, dozens of men made their way on horseback into Montana and traversed along the Yellowstone River and around Yellowstone Lake.

sentences.cn_text: 当年秋天，他们在怀俄明州的布里杰堡结束了此次考察。
sentences.en_text: That fall, they concluded the survey in Fort Bridger, Wyoming.

sentences.cn_text: 尽管美洲原住民（以及后来的矿工与毛皮猎人）早已认识到该地区物产丰饶，但大多数美国人对此却一无所知。
sentences.en_text: Though Native Americans (and later miners and fur trappers) had long recognized the area’s riches, most Americans did not.

sentences.cn_text: 正因如此，海登的探险队旨在更全面地认识黄石河地区——从温泉、瀑布到各类动植物，无所不包。
sentences.en_text: That’s why Hayden’s expedition aimed to produce a fuller understanding of the Yellowstone River region, from its hot springs and waterfalls to its variety of flora and fauna.

sentences.cn_text: 随行人员除了科学家之外，还有艺术家：画家托马斯·莫兰与摄影师威廉·亨利·杰克逊肩负着记录这一惊人自然美景并将其展示给世人的使命。
sentences.en_text: In addition to the entourage of scientists, the team also included artists: Painter Thomas Moran and photographer William Henry Jackson were charged with capturing this astounding natural beauty and sharing it with the world.

sentences.cn_text: 该法案获得广泛支持，在国会以压倒性多数顺利通过。
sentences.en_text: The bill proved largely popular and sailed through Congress with large majorities in favor.

sentences.cn_text: 1872年初，参众两院相继通过了保护黄石地区的立法。
sentences.en_text: In quick succession, the Senate and House passed legislation protecting Yellowstone in early 1872.

sentences.cn_text: 同年三月，总统尤利西斯·S·格兰特签署法案，正式将黄石设立为世界上第一座国家公园。
sentences.en_text: That March, President Ulysses S. Grant signed an act into law that established Yellowstone as the world’s first national park.

sentences.cn_text: 虽有部分当地居民反对这一指定，但这一决定总体上仍被广泛接受——而杰克逊的照片在这场保护该地区的斗争中发挥了关键作用。
sentences.en_text: While some locals opposed to the designation, the decision was largely accepted — and Jackson’s photos played a key role in the fight to protect the area.

sentences.cn_text: “我认为，若没有那些影像，法律保护恐怕不会在那样的时间内得以实现，”记者兼《先知与巨头，护林员与流氓，野牛与熊：国家公园管理局百年史》一书作者希瑟·汉森如是说。
sentences.en_text: “I don’t believe that the legal protection would have happened in the timeframe that it did without those images,” says Heather Hansen, journalist and author of Prophets and Moguls, Rangers and Rogues, Bison and Bears:100 Years of the National Park Service.

sentences.cn_text: 也许最为重要的是，这些影像为公园景观提供了实证记录，并最终呈送到政府官员手中。
sentences.en_text: Perhaps most importantly, the images provided documentary evidence of the park’s sights that later made its way to government officials.

sentences.cn_text: 探险结束数周后，海登将团队的观察所得汇编成一份详尽的报告，力图说服参众两院议员，以及内政部等政府机构的同僚，让他们相信黄石理应得到保护。
sentences.en_text: Weeks after completing the expedition, Hayden collected his team’s observations into an extensive report aimed at convincing senators and representatives, along with colleagues at government agencies like the Department of the Interior, that Yellowstone ought to be preserved.
